elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 1,000,000 per occurrence.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence".

elements.element: Commercial general liability coverage is at least USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate.
elements.evidence: Inserted clause: "and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate" for CGL.

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: "professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000".

elements.element: If Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 5,000,000.
elements.evidence: "where TrueLink processes any data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Client, cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000" — trigger covers every category of Customer data, not selected named types.

elements.element: Vendor maintains workers' compensation coverage as required by law.
elements.evidence: "and workers' compensation insurance as required by law".

elements.element: Vendor provides certificates of insurance on request.
elements.evidence: "TrueLink shall provide certificates of insurance on request."

elements.element: Professional errors and omissions coverage is at least USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: E&O of not less than USD 2,000,000 exceeds the USD 1,000,000 fallback floor.

elements.element: Cyber and privacy coverage is at least USD 2,000,000.
elements.evidence: Cyber and privacy liability of not less than USD 5,000,000 exceeds the USD 2,000,000 fallback floor.

reasons: All six preferred elements appear in the inserted operative sentence with the correct amounts, bases and party direction (TrueLink as insuring party, Client as beneficiary of the data trigger).

The insertion omits the model language's extras — "at its own expense" and the one-year survival tail — consistent with the instruction that such model-language additions are non-minimal unless a selected element requires them.

The cyber trigger is drafted as "any data belonging to, supplied by or processed for Client," satisfying the requirement that the Customer Data insurance trigger cover every category rather than named data types.

Retained Section 30 (force majeure) is untouched; no words outside the target elements were deleted or paraphrased, and the new stand-alone insurance paragraph creates no undefined term or dangling cross-reference ("TrueLink" and "Client" are defined in the preamble).

Concise insertion for a genuinely missing clause: deterministic checks confirm no pre-existing insurance obligation elsewhere, so wholly new wording is appropriate and no duplicate operative coverage is created.
